battle.name: 漢攻大宛之戰
battle.brief: 公元前104年（太初元年），漢廷以大宛拒交汗血馬為由，遣李廣利率屬國六千騎與郡國惡少年數萬人自敦煌西征，越鹽水攻郁成城，主力受挫後趙破奴以敢死數百人奇襲破城、斬郁成王。卡面的埃及長矛屬青銅時代工藝，與本役相隔三千年，不在此役現場；同期漢軍近身用環首刀與鐵矛，大宛則以弓矢彎刀守城。

kit.name: 埃及長矛
kit.history: 早王朝時期的長矛，銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上。埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。

countries: 這場戰爭是西漢中央對中亞費爾干納盆地大宛國的一次軍事逼迫，發生在漢武帝太初元年（公元前104年）。漢朝一方由中央直轄的貳師將軍李廣利率領，配以屬國歸附部落的騎兵與郡國調發的「惡少年」步卒，是漢朝西域戰爭中少數把騎兵、步卒與大批隨軍牲畜綁在一起投入的遠征行動；《史記》記載此次出動的兵員為屬國六千騎、郡國惡少年數萬人，隨軍牛羊驢騾駱數十萬匹，另齎絹二千匹作為賞賜與賄賂之用，並派數千屬國兵充當前導「候」，先期偵察道路。大宛一方控制著費爾干納河谷的城邑與草場，《史記·大宛列傳》稱其「控弦有五萬餘」，是漢朝在塔里木盆地南北兩側之外遇到的又一個有相當兵力的城邦國家。戰役牽動的第三方並非單一盟友：大宛王在郁成失守後西逃康居（塞種人控制的河中一帶），漢廷因此派持節使者往康居、大月氏、安息索取良馬並追索大宛王，安息與康居皆遣使應對，匈奴則在漢使西行的路上不斷劫掠，使漢朝通往西域的道路始終處於威脅之下。這樣的格局意味著，漢朝此役雖然只以大宛為直接打擊對象，實際上是在西域交通與使團往返的問題上，向中亞與北亞的幾個勢力同時施壓。
countriesEn: This war was a military coercion by the Western Han court against the state of Dayuan in the Fergana basin of Central Asia, fought in the first year of Taichu (104 BC) under Emperor Wu of Han. The Han side was led by the Ershi General Li Guangli, with cavalry supplied by the states that had submitted to the empire and foot soldiers levied from the commanderies and kingdoms as 'bad boys'; it was one of the few Han campaigns in the western regions to commit cavalry, infantry and a huge drove of baggage animals together. The Shiji records the force as six thousand cavalry of the dependent states plus several tens of thousands of 'bad boys' from the commanderies, accompanied by several hundred thousand head of cattle, sheep, donkeys, mules and camels, with two thousand bolts of silk carried along as rewards and gifts, and several thousand dependent-state troops detailed as advance guides (hou) to scout the road ahead. Dayuan controlled the towns and pastures of the Fergana valley, and the Shiji liezhuan of Dayuan describes it as having more than fifty thousand men under bow-strings, which made it the first city-state of comparable strength the Han met beyond the Tarim basin on either flank. The campaign drew in not one but several third parties: after Yucheng fell, the king of Dayuan fled west to Kangju, the land of the Saka around the middle Oxus, and the court accordingly sent envoys bearing tally-tubes to Kangju, to the Great Yuezhi and to Anxi to demand the fine horses and to press for the surrender of the fugitive king; Anxi and Kangju both sent envoys in reply, while Xiongnu raiders repeatedly intercepted Han envoys on the road, keeping the western route itself permanently under threat. The pattern means that although Dayuan was the only direct target, the Han were in fact pressing several Central and North Asian powers at once over the question of traffic along the western corridor and the safety of their embassies.
people: 決定這場戰爭走向的是漢武帝劉徹。他聽聞大宛善馬藏在貳師城，先後派使者持節持金往贖，遭拒之後又聽從曾出使大宛的姚定漢等人「兵不過三千人，彊弩射之即破宛城」的估計，下令拜李廣利為貳師將軍，開啟西征；主帥李廣利是靠入宮掖得寵而發跡的外戚將領，此前並無在西域帶兵攻城的前例，他既要對天子交代期限，又要面對一個控弦五萬餘、坐擁費爾干納城邑的國家。真正扭轉戰局的是趙破奴，他以敢死數百人為先鋒奇襲郁成，破城擒斬郁成王，使西征不至於全軍潰散；後來史官把郁成城破的功勞記在他名下，漢書亦以他為破奴將軍。大宛方面，郁成王死於破城之後，大宛王則帶殘部西走康居，留在費爾干納的臣屬與城邑後來不得不向漢朝謝罪並獻出良馬。漢使車令在索要馬匹時受辱，椎金馬而去，等於親手把一場可以談判解決的索馬糾紛推成開戰的理由；而大宛、安息與康居各自派來的使者，則是把戰場內的勝負再帶回中亞外交場合的關鍵人物。
peopleEn: The decision to fight was Emperor Wu of Han's, Liu Che. On learning that the fine horses of Dayuan were kept in the city of Ershi, he sent envoys with tally-tubes and gold to buy them, and after the refusal acted on the estimate of Yao Dingan and other men who had served as envoys to Dayuan that three thousand Han soldiers and strong crossbows would suffice to break the city, and appointed Li Guangli Ershi General to open the western campaign. Li Guangli was a favourite at court who had risen through palace connections and had no prior record of campaigning or storming towns in the western regions; he was answerable to the throne for the schedule he had accepted, and he faced a state of some fifty thousand bow-armed men holding the fortified towns of Fergana. The man who actually turned the battle was Zhao Ponu, who led several hundred dare-to-die men as the assault column in a surprise attack on Yucheng, broke the walls, and took the king of Yucheng, which kept the expedition from collapsing entirely; the later historian credited the fall of Yucheng to him under the title Ponu General, and the Hanshu likewise records him as a general. On the Dayuan side, the king of Yucheng was killed when the city was stormed and the king of Dayuan withdrew with the remnants of his forces to Kangju, while the dependent towns and households left in Fergana had no choice but to make their peace with the Han and hand over horses. The Han envoy Che Ling, rebuffed while demanding the horses, beat the golden horse to pieces and left, converting a quarrel that could have been settled by negotiation into the stated pretext for war; and the envoys dispatched by Dayuan, Anxi and Kangju carried the result of the fighting on the field back into Central Asian diplomacy.
kits: 卡面這件埃及長矛屬於青銅時代早期的工藝：長杆木質，前端裝銅或青銅的矛頭，形制簡潔，用途是守城與近身刺擊。它與公元前104年的郁成之戰相隔約三千一百年，在本場戰役中不可能出現，戰場上真正交手的兵器另有其物。漢軍遠征軍的近身冷兵器以環首刀與鐵矛為主，弓弩則是最被倚重的遠程殺傷手段——姚定漢勸漢武帝出兵時強調的就是漢軍的強弩可以壓制城頭，漢軍在攻城中以強弩陣先行覆蓋城牆與城門，再以步卒持矛、刀接近，登城後靠刀、矛解決守軍；李廣利、趙破奴所部的騎兵使用北方草原式的良馬，配馬鞍、馬鐙與皮革馬具，騎射是騎兵的基本技能，用來打擊城郊游擊與追擊潰兵。攻城的實際手段是突襲而非器械：趙破奴以數百敢死為先鋒，在主力抵達前逼近城壁，破門而入，形成破城屠掠、斬郁成王的結果。兩軍的後勤同樣關鍵，漢軍隨軍攜帶數十萬匹牛羊驢騾駱作肉食與馱載，齎絹二千匹是賞賜與收買人心的物資；大宛與其周邊則以弓矢、反曲彎刀、皮甲與土築城牆守備，控制水源與城郊草場是他們抵禦遠征軍的關鍵。雙方爭奪的最終目標其實是一種馬：天馬、汗血馬，漢廷要的是這些馬，不是郁成城本身。
kitsEn: The Egyptian spear on the card belongs to early Bronze Age craftwork: a long wooden shaft with a copper or bronze head fitted to its front, a plain form built for defending walls and for stabbing at close quarters. It stands roughly three thousand one hundred years away from the battle of Yucheng in 104 BC and could not have been present in it; the weapons that actually met on the field were entirely different matters. The close combat arms of the Han expedition were ring-pommel sabres and iron spears, while the bow and the crossbow were the ranged killing tools they relied on most; it was precisely the strength of the Han crossbow that Yao Dingan invoked when he advised the emperor to attack, Han archers covering the walls and gates with massed crossbow volleys before spearmen and sabre-men closed to storm the ramparts. The cavalry of Li Guangli and Zhao Ponu rode horses of the northern steppe kind, fitted with saddles, stirrups and leather harness, and the basic skill of a trooper was shooting from the saddle, used both in hit-and-run attacks outside the walls and in the pursuit of routed defenders. The method of taking the city was a surprise, not a siege engine: Zhao Ponu brought several hundred dare-to-dies up to the walls before the main body arrived, broke the gate, and carried the city by storm, which is how the king of Yucheng came to be cut down. Logistics mattered as much as weapons: the Han marched with several hundred thousand head of cattle, sheep, donkeys, mules and camels for meat and pack transport, and the two thousand bolts of silk were both reward and bribe. Dayuan and its neighbours defended with arrows, recurved sabres, leather armour and mud-built walls, and control of water and of the grazing grounds outside the town was their key against a distant besieging army. What both sides were really after, in the end, was horses: the tianma and the blood-sweating horses of Fergana. What the Han court wanted was the horses, not the city of Yucheng.
tactics: 漢軍的部署是典型的西域遠征形制：主力沿敦煌西出的唯一通道前進，屬國騎兵與先行「候」分批前出探路，隊伍以步騎混編，行軍縱隊拉得很長，牲畜與給養夾在中間，行進速度因此受制於最慢的環節。真正的難題是水與草：鹽水一帶（西域中部的鹽澤，即今羅布泊周邊）地勢乾涸、井泉稀少，隊伍越過此段時多有掉隊與非戰減員，等到接近郁成，人馬已嚴重疲憊，司馬遷記下「數十萬眾，上崗者不過數千」，說明遠征大軍在攻城時能投入的突擊兵力其實有限，這也是李廣利在郁成城下初戰受挫的原因之一。趙破奴的解法是縮減接戰面：不與主力和守軍正面消耗，只取數百敢死逼近城垣，選擇守軍戒備最鬆的時機突入，破門、屠掠、斬王，一氣完成，前104年的戰事因此以小規模奇襲收束，主力仍在城外待機。漢朝這邊在戰場之外同樣用兵：使者持節往康居、大月氏、安息索取良馬並施壓，試圖用外交手段讓大宛的盟友孤立，並借大宛內部對漢朝的恐懼，換取馬匹與降附。大宛的戰術則是守城待援與騎兵游擊並行，倚仗費爾干納城牆、水源與通往康居的道路，把持久戰交給西方盟友。
tacticsEn: The Han deployment was the standard pattern for a far-western expedition: the main body advanced along the single road leading west out of Dunhuang, the cavalry of the dependent states and the advance 'hou' went ahead in batches to scout the route, and the column was mixed infantry and cavalry with the baggage animals and the provisions carried in the middle, so that the speed of the march was set by its slowest element. The real difficulty was water and fodder: the salt-water belt of the central western regions, the salt desert around what is now the Lop Nor, was dry and poor in wells, and the column lost men and animals to thirst and desertion while crossing it; by the time it reached Yucheng the troops were worn out, and Sima Qian's note that 'of the tens of thousands of troops, no more than a few thousand went up the slope' shows how few of the men of a great expedition could actually be committed to the storming of the walls, which is one of the reasons for Li Guangli's first failure before the city. Zhao Ponu's answer was to reduce the front: rather than wear down the defenders with his main body, he took only several hundred dare-to-dies up to the rampart, chose the moment when the watch was slackest, broke in, sacked the town and cut off the king, completing the whole business in a single stroke. The fighting of 104 BC thus ended in a small-scale surprise while the main army still lay outside the walls. The Han were fighting on the diplomatic front at the same time, sending envoys with tally-tubes to Kangju, the Great Yuezhi and Anxi to demand the horses and to apply pressure, hoping to isolate Dayuan's allies and to exploit the fear the Dayuan people had taken from the Han, and buying both the horses and the submission. Dayuan's own method was to hold the town and wait for help while the cavalry harassed the besiegers, relying on the walls of Fergana, on the water supply and on the road to Kangju to hand the war of endurance over to its western allies.
data: 有根據可寫的數字大致如下。此次西征的兵員，據《史記·大宛列傳》，為屬國六千騎及郡國惡少年數萬人；隨軍牛羊驢騾駱數十萬匹，齎絹二千匹，另有屬國數千人充當先導「候」。出征的起點在敦煌，漢軍自此西行數千里，穿越鹽水一帶的鹽澤荒漠，抵達大宛境內的郁成城下時，士卒饑渴疲憊，書中記為「數十萬眾，上崗者不過數千」。大宛方面的兵力，《史記》稱其「控弦有五萬餘」。戰果方面，前104年秋季出發，入冬前後打下郁成城，郁成王被斬，大宛王西逃康居；出兵的確切月份在傳世史籍中沒有明確記載，卡面標為十月，取的是秋季出兵的通說。真正解決馬匹問題的是前101年（太初四年）李廣利再率的第二次遠征：漢軍再圍大宛王城貳師城，長期封鎖水源與糧道，最後破城屠掠，奪取良馬，李廣利因功益封二千石。從首次出兵到攻下王城，前後約三年。若以里程計，敦煌至郁成的直線距離就接近四千里，漢軍的實際行程遠遠多於此。全戰役中漢廷取得的良馬數量有限，均以十數匹計，遠不足以成軍。
dataEn: The figures that can be given on good authority are roughly these. The strength of the expedition, according to the Shiji liezhuan of Dayuan, was six thousand cavalry of the dependent states together with several tens of thousands of 'bad boys' from the commanderies and kingdoms; several hundred thousand head of cattle, sheep, donkeys, mules and camels went with them, together with two thousand bolts of silk, and several thousand dependent-state troops were detailed as advance scouts. The point of departure was Dunhuang, from which the Han marched westward for several thousand li, crossing the salt desert of the salt-water region, and when they reached Yucheng in Dayuan's territory the men were hungry, thirsty and exhausted, the book recording that 'of the tens of thousands of troops, no more than a few thousand went up the slope'. Dayuan's own strength, the Shiji says, was 'more than fifty thousand under bow-strings'. As for results, the army set out in the autumn of 104 BC and took Yucheng around the turn of the winter, the king of Yucheng being cut down and the king of Dayuan fleeing west to Kangju; the exact month of departure is not recorded in the transmitted histories, and the card gives October, which is the generally accepted reading of an autumn dispatch. What actually settled the question of the horses was the second expedition led by Li Guangli in 101 BC, the fourth year of Taichu: the Han again ringed the capital of Dayuan, the city of Ershi, sealed off its water and grain for a long time, and at last stormed the city and sacked it, taking the fine horses, Li Guangli being raised with an additional fief of two thousand shi for his service. From the first departure to the fall of the capital, three years passed. Measured as distance, the direct line from Dunhuang to Yucheng is close to four thousand li, and the army's actual route was very much longer. The number of fine horses the Han court obtained was small, of the order of a dozen or so, nowhere near enough to form a body of cavalry.
cause: 直接起因是一批馬。大宛的良馬在中原被稱為汗血馬、天馬，盛產於費爾干納的馬群，是天子輦下與軍陣都急需的坐騎；漢朝先後聽聞大宛有善馬寄存在貳師城，便派使者持節、持金往贖。大宛王不肯交付，理由也說得直白：漢朝離得太遠，路上鹽水多有敗亡，北面有匈奴寇掠，南面缺水缺草，漢使往來本身就有去無回。漢使車令在索要時受辱，椎金馬而去，漢廷聞訊大怒；此前也有多名使者在往返途中死亡或為匈奴所執。加上曾出使大宛的姚定漢等人以「漢兵不過三千人，彊弩射之即破宛城」相勸，開戰的決策就這樣形成。深一層看，這場戰爭是漢武帝經營西域的必然副產品：西漢在漠北打垮匈奴後，匈奴控制的西域通道對漢使與商旅構成持續威脅，漢朝若不能打通從敦煌到塔里木、再到費爾干納的交通線，使團與馬匹的交換就沒有保障；同時漢廷在西南剛平定南越，在關中又面臨財政與轉運的壓力，此時對外用兵一旦受阻，前線與後方都會被拖長，因此漢武帝寧願集中兵馬再打一次大宛，以求一勞永逸地換到馬與通道。
causeEn: The immediate cause was a batch of horses. Dayuan's fine horses, known in the central plains as the blood-sweating horses and the heavenly horses, were raised in the herds of Fergana, and the animals the Son of Heaven rode in his carriage and the horses the armies fought on were in acute need of them; having heard that Dayuan kept good horses in the city of Ershi, the Han court sent envoys with tally-tubes and gold to buy them. The king of Dayuan refused to hand them over, and gave his reasons plainly: the Han were too far away, the route through the salt-water country was attended by constant loss of life, there were Xiongnu raiders to the north and no water or pasture to the south, and the envoys who came and went were often never seen again. The Han envoy Che Ling, being rebuffed when he asked for the horses, beat the golden horse to pieces and left, and the court was furious when it heard; before that, several envoys had died on the road or been taken prisoner by the Xiongnu. Adding the advice of Yao Dingan and the others who had served in Dayuan, that three thousand Han soldiers with strong crossbows would break the city in a trice, the decision to go to war was made. At a deeper level the war was the inevitable by-product of Emperor Wu's management of the western regions: after beating the Xiongnu in the northern steppe, the Han found that the routes through the western regions, which the Xiongnu controlled, remained a standing threat to Han envoys and merchants, and unless the corridor from Dunhuang through the Tarim basin to Fergana could be opened, neither the exchange of envoys nor the transfer of horses had any security. At the same time the court had only just settled the kingdom of Nanyue in the south-west and faced pressure on its finances and its transport in the Guanzhong region, and once a war on the frontier had stalled, both the front line and the rear would be stretched out; Emperor Wu therefore preferred to concentrate troops and hit Dayuan once more, in the hope of buying the horses and the corridor in a single stroke.
impact: 郁成城破之後，漢朝在西域的處境明顯改觀。大宛在費爾干納的統一度被打破，國勢從獨立的城邦國家轉為向漢廷低頭的附庸：其臣屬與城市陸續歸附，向漢朝謝罪並獻上良馬，漢使得以持節西行，把觸角從敦煌一路伸到康居、大月氏、安息，與安息建立了直接的馬匹與使節往來。這條線後來成為絲路北道與天山南北交通網的骨架；從前104年破郁成、前101年屠貳師城，到前60年設西域都護，漢朝在天山兩側的經營是逐段推進的，這場戰爭是第一段。馬匹同樣改變了漢朝的軍力結構：汗血馬、天馬進入長安後，漢廷把馬政與畜牧提到極重要的位置，邊郡的馬苑、郡國的養馬與軍中騎兵的比重都因此調整，後來衛青、霍去病在漠北作戰時能以輕騎迂迴、分割匈奴，正是建立在這段時間積累的馬匹與騎兵經驗之上。另一面的代價也很快浮現：遠征耗費巨大，「勞師遠征」之議在昭帝時被賢良文學反覆引用，成為鹽鐵會議批判武帝用兵的核心論據之一。漢朝在中亞的勝利因此同時帶來兩種後果，一種是通道與馬匹，另一種是財政與民力被拉長的消耗。
impactEn: After the fall of Yucheng the Han position in the western regions visibly changed. Dayuan's unity in Fergana was broken, and the state shifted from an independent city-state to a subordinate that bowed to the court: its dependent towns and cities came over one by one, made their peace and offered the good horses, and Han envoys could travel west with tally-tubes, stretching the line of contact from Dunhuang all the way to Kangju, the Great Yuezhi and Anxi, and opening direct exchanges of horses and envoys with Anxi. That line later became the backbone of the northern Silk Road and of the transport network across the Tian Shan; the Han advance on both sides of the mountains was made step by step, and this war was the first step of it, from breaking Yucheng in 104 BC and sacking Ershi in 101 BC to the establishment of the Protectorate of the Western Regions in 60 BC. The horses changed the shape of Han military power as well: the blood-sweating and heavenly horses reached Chang'an, and the court raised horse administration and stockbreeding to a place of the first importance, adjusting the stud-farms of the frontier commanderies, the raising of horses by commandery and kingdom, and the proportion of cavalry in the armies. The ability of Wei Qing and Huo Qubing to ride light forces round and behind the Xiongnu in the northern steppe was built on the horses and the cavalry experience accumulated over these years. The cost came up quickly on the other side: the cost of campaigning far from home was argued repeatedly by the scholars and worthies of the reign of Emperor Zhao, and became one of the central charges brought against Emperor Wu's wars at the Salt and Iron Discourses. The Han victory in Central Asia therefore carried two consequences at once, a corridor and a supply of horses on the one hand, and a prolongation of the drain on the treasury and on the strength of the people on the other.
result: 就公元前104年這一場而言，結果是明確的：漢軍攻下郁成城，斬郁成王，大宛王西走康居，費爾干納的城邑與臣屬多被迫向漢朝歸附，漢廷沒有在這一年拿到馬，卻打開了通往大宛腹地的通道，也拿下了下一次取馬的立足點。真正的收官在三年之後：前101年（太初四年），李廣利率領的第二次大軍進抵大宛王城貳師城，長期圍困並封鎖城中水源與糧道，破城後屠掠，奪取良馬，軍中議功，李廣利益封二千石；大宛自此再無獨抗漢廷之力，漢朝的西域通道由敦煌直抵費爾干納。整個過程裡，漢朝的戰爭手段是「先以奇襲取點、再以大軍壓城」，配合持節使者向康居、大月氏、安息施壓的外交，加上誘敵於鹽水一線的殘酷消耗，最終換來汗血馬與通道。對中原的馬政與西域的經營而言，這場戰爭是一次付出巨大而收益明確的遠征：它沒有徹底解決漢朝在西域的治理難題，卻為後來設西域都護、經營天山南北的諸侯國，鋪好了自敦煌直抵大宛的交通線。
resultEn: For the year 104 BC itself the outcome is clear: the Han took Yucheng, the king of Yucheng was cut down, the king of Dayuan fled west to Kangju, and the towns and dependants of Fergana were forced to submit to the Han; the court did not obtain the horses that year, but it opened the road into the heart of Dayuan and gained the foothold from which the next seizure of horses would be made. The real conclusion came three years later: in 101 BC, the fourth year of Taichu, the second Han army led by Li Guangli reached the capital of Dayuan at Ershi, held it in a long siege while sealing off the water and the grain inside, stormed the city and sacked it, taking the fine horses, and when the campaign was reckoned up Li Guangli was granted an additional fief of two thousand shi; from that point Dayuan had no strength left to stand alone against the Han, and the Han corridor ran straight from Dunhuang to Fergana. Through the whole business the Han method was to take a point first by surprise and then to press the city with a great army, supported by envoys with tally-tubes applying pressure on Kangju, the Great Yuezhi and Anxi, and adding the harsh attrition of the salt-water country to it, and in the end this bought the blood-sweating horses and the corridor. For the horse administration of the central plains and for the Han presence in the western regions, this war was a costly and clearly profitable expedition: it did not solve the problem of governing the western regions, but it paved the way from Dunhuang to Dayuan for the later establishment of the Protectorate of the Western Regions and the management of the states south and north of the Tian Shan.
